periods.analysis: At 16,742,306 annual enplaned passengers, Harborview International is yellow against the 18,000,000 target, and this quarter is our baseline for the recovery arc. My read is that demand is healthy but still not fully converted into boarded seats, especially on late-evening departures where airline crew availability and aircraft utilization are constraining capacity. The strongest pockets were the coastal leisure banks and the Port Connector business markets, while the watch-item is weekday load factor softness on the Midwest and Mountain routes. Operations held together well through the summer peak, but yellow is the right call until we see durable seat growth, not just fuller airplanes.
periods.recommendations: Keep the Air Service Development team focused on converting the fall schedule: secure written commitments from the top five carriers for added frequencies on the ORD, DEN, ATL, DFW, and SFO routes. Have Airport Operations and TSA complete a gate-by-gate turn review at Concourses B and C so added capacity does not create avoidable queueing. Track weekly booked-load trends for the first 6 a.m. departure bank and the 8-10 p.m. recovery bank as the specific watch-item.

periods.analysis: Annual enplaned passengers rose to 17,555,089, up 812,783 from 16,742,306, which is real progress but still yellow below the 18,000,000 target. The holiday schedule helped, and the new Harborview-Bogotá and restored Harborview-Minneapolis frequencies gave us more lift in the right markets. We are no longer talking about a fragile recovery; we are talking about the last 444,911 passengers needed to clear target. The risk is that winter irregular operations can give back gains quickly if deicing, baggage sort, and gate recovery are not tightly managed.
periods.recommendations: Lock in the winter operating playbook now: pre-stage deicing trucks on Pads 2 and 4, extend baggage sort staffing on Friday and Sunday peaks, and require daily 6 a.m. carrier station calls through January. Use the Q4 gain to press carriers for spring break seat additions instead of one-time holiday capacity. Continue the weekly route profitability packet for DEN, MCO, MSP, and Bogotá so the airlines see Harborview as a reliable add-market, not a seasonal bet.

periods.analysis: This quarter crossed the line: annual enplaned passengers reached 18,479,241, up 924,152 from 17,555,089, and the measure is green above the 18,000,000 target. That is the result of both market demand and disciplined execution, especially the January-April gate-use reset that reduced late gate holds in Concourse C. The international bank also performed well, with Bogotá maturing and the London shoulder-season loads coming in stronger than expected. I am pleased, but not self-satisfied; a green airport still has to protect reliability before it courts more passengers.
periods.recommendations: Sustain the green by converting the temporary Gate C12/C14 common-use protocol into the standard spring operating plan. Extend the carrier incentive program only to routes that add net new seats outside the already-congested 7-9 a.m. bank. Start design authorization for the North Checkpoint queuing re-striping so passenger growth does not outrun front-door processing.

periods.analysis: Annual enplaned passengers fell to 17,436,050, down 1,043,191 from 18,479,241, moving us back to yellow. Some of this is the rolling-year math after a strong prior quarter, but the operational story is clear: spring capacity was thinner than forecast when two carriers pulled aircraft for engine inspections and trimmed Harborview turns first. The airport remained reliable, yet we did not have enough seats in market to hold green. The watch-item is summer schedule integrity, particularly whether the added West Coast and Florida frequencies actually operate as filed.
periods.recommendations: Put the summer schedule under a weekly variance review comparing filed seats, operated seats, cancellations, and completed turns by carrier. Have Air Service Development escalate with carriers that reduced Harborview first, using the Concourse C performance data and regional demand forecasts to argue for restoration. Keep the North Checkpoint re-striping moving, but do not open new peak-hour promotions unless TSA lane staffing is confirmed.

periods.analysis: The yellow position tightened further: annual enplaned passengers declined to 16,518,486, down 917,564 from 17,436,050, leaving us just above the 16,500,000 red threshold. That is too close to the floor for my comfort, even though summer passenger processing and airfield performance were stable. The main drag was capacity, not appetite: airline schedule cuts after the Pratt engine groundings hit our medium-haul routes, and the temporary closure of Taxiway K for pavement panels limited recovery options during thunderstorm days. This is a concerned-but-managed quarter, and the watch-item is avoiding any slide below 16,500,000 while we rebuild Q4 lift.
periods.recommendations: Stand up a 60-day Passenger Recovery Room with Aviation, the carriers, TSA, concessions, and ground handlers meeting every Tuesday until the winter schedule is locked. Prioritize restoration on the ORD, DEN, LAS, and MCO routes where local demand is measurable and leakage to competing airports is highest. Finish Taxiway K panel work before the Thanksgiving push and publish a carrier confidence bulletin with completion photos, NOTAM closure history, and recovered taxi-time data.

periods.analysis: We pulled away from the edge this quarter: annual enplaned passengers increased to 17,395,285, up 876,799 from 16,518,486, though the measure remains yellow below target. The recovery room did what it was supposed to do, converting winter schedule commitments into operated seats and tightening the Sunday evening baggage and gate plan. Holiday demand was strong across the Florida, Texas, and Caribbean markets, and the seaport cruise-air packages helped fill midweek inbound banks. We still need another 604,715 passengers to reach green, so the watch-item is whether Q1 business travel and international growth can carry the momentum.
periods.recommendations: Keep the Passenger Recovery Room active through spring break, but narrow it to carrier capacity, TSA throughput, and ground-handler staffing decisions. Extend the cruise-air coordination with the Port Authority by publishing shared arrival forecasts for Saturdays and Sundays at least 21 days out. Offer targeted landing-fee credits only for net-new Q1 frequencies that operate at least 85% of scheduled flights.

periods.analysis: Annual enplaned passengers reached 18,351,369, up 956,084 from 17,395,285, returning the measure to green above the 18,000,000 target. This is the better kind of green because it came from restored frequencies, international maturity, and cleaner execution at the curb, checkpoint, and gate. The North Checkpoint re-striping and the Concourse B tow-team pilot reduced the friction that passengers feel even when the dashboard only shows volume. We have rebuilt confidence after the 2025 dip, and now the job is to hold the base while adding service selectively.
periods.recommendations: Make the Concourse B tow-team pilot permanent for the 5-8 a.m. departure bank and add a second tug crew on peak Mondays. Sustain the North Checkpoint layout through the summer and use queue cameras to trigger staffing calls before wait times spill into the ticketing hall. Begin formal talks with two transcontinental carriers and one Latin America carrier, but condition incentives on year-round service rather than summer-only lift.

periods.analysis: Annual enplaned passengers eased to 17,532,366, down 819,003 from 18,351,369, moving back to yellow but staying comfortably above the red threshold. The quarter looks like a seasonal and capacity-driven step down rather than a demand break, with early-summer leisure strong but several weekday business markets still below the Q1 run rate. Weather also mattered: two June tidal-flooding events around the airport access road did not close the terminal, but they did disrupt employee and passenger arrival patterns during the morning bank. The watch-item is keeping operated seats and landside reliability aligned so this yellow does not become a second-half drift.
periods.recommendations: Activate the airport landside flood playbook before the next king-tide window: pre-position shuttle buses at Lot E, stage traffic control at Seaport Boulevard, and push carrier employee reporting advisories 12 hours ahead. Require carriers to submit July-August operated-seat confirmations by route, with special attention to ORD, DEN, SFO, and MCO. Sustain the green-era service disciplines that worked in Q1, including the tow-team and checkpoint queue triggers, while targeting one fall business-market frequency restoration.

periods.analysis: Annual enplaned passengers rose from 17,532,366 to 18,050,000, just above the 18,000,000 target. The recovery restores the measure to green, although the margin is narrow.
periods.recommendations: Keep checking operated seats and airport access reliability so the recovery holds through the next quarter.
